newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Applied Materials to buy Opal, Orbot.
newsitem.headline: Applied Materials to buy Opal, Orbot.

text.p: Applied Materials, a leading maker of equipment used to produce computer chips, said Monday it has a definitive agreement to acquire two related Israeli companies -- Opal Inc. and Orbot Instruments Ltd. -- for about $285 million.
Combined, the acquisitions are the biggest ever in the high-technology sector in Israel.

Applied Materials said it would buy Orbot, a supplier of wafer inspection systems, for about $110 million in cash, and Opal, a leading supplier of semiconductor test equipment, for about $175 million.
Orbotech owns 14 percent, or 1.2 million shares of Opal.
Applied Materials said it expected to commence a cash tender offer by Nov. 27 for Opal at $18.50 per share. Opal will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Santa Clara, Calif.-based company.

Major shareholders in Orbot are Ormat Industries Ltd., a leading industrial holding company, and Carroll Acquisition Corp., owned by U.S. businessman William Davidson. Together they hold about 16 percent of Orbot's shares, said Zvi Lapidot, Orbot's chairman.
Israel's Clal Electronics Industries, a subsidiary of Clal Industries, will receive $50 million for the sale of its roughly 30 percent stake in Opal.
Orbotech, which makes automated optical inspection systems used in the manufacture of printed circuit boards, will receive about $15.5 million after-tax for its stake in Opal.
Orbotech has agreed to vote in favour of the merger and sell its holdings in Opal to Applied Materials, it said.
Applied Materials said the acquisitions were in line with the company's goal to become a leader in the metrology and inspection markets.

"What the core is in this business is pattern recognition, optics and artificial intelligence," Dennis Hunter, Applied Materials managing director, corporate development, told a Tel Aviv news conference. "These are things in which we are not experienced. These are things in which Israel has a superb tradition of excellence."
Applied Materials said it expected the acquisitions to result in a first-quarter pre-tax charge of $50 million to $60 million, or 27 cents to 32 cents a share after-tax.
Hunter said the deal was expected to close in about a month.
